newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Netanyahu stands firm on security.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Netanyahu stands firm on security.

text.p: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu told U.S. envoy Dennis Ross on Sunday there could be no progress on Middle East peace until the Palestinian Authority cracks down on militants, an Israeli cabinet statement said.

It said Netanyahu had told the cabinet he had informed Ross that "without any fundamental change on the part of the Palestinian Authority in dealing with security issues, the diplomatic process will not be able to advance".
President Bill Clinton sent Ross to the region to try to reinvigorate peacemaking after a double suicide bombing in Jerusalem on July 30 killed 15 people, including the two Islamic militant bombers.
Netanyahu responded to the attack with the closure of the West Bank and Gaza Strip and other punitive measures, saying Palestinian President Yasser Arafat had failed to clamp down on extremists.

"In order to make it possible to advance in the diplomatic process, the Palestinian Authority must deal with the problem of terrorism," the statement said. It also denied assertions by Arafat that Israeli officers had told him the bombers came from abroad.
Ross, who has said his mission focuses on security, met Netanyahu in Jerusalem on Sunday morning and later held talks with Arafat in the self-ruled West Bank town of Ramallah.
